I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, this is the system I know best, the machinery fits it, the buyers are steady, and the risk is lower than trying something fancy. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will focus on managing it well through jointing, heading, and grain filling, then I will harvest it and quickly plant summer maize on the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I care about stable yield more than saving seed. I will not push fertilizer too hard, because too much nitrogen raises cost and can cause lodging or waste. I will irrigate when the crop most needs water, not blindly. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before wheat where needed, and after wheat harvest I will keep the turnaround fast for maize, using lighter tillage so I do not miss soil moisture. For pests and diseases, I will spray only as many times as needed to protect yield, mainly for the common problems in wheat and maize. My goal is steady output, manageable labor, and reliable cash income, so I will stay with the crops and practices I trust most.
